control_implications.headline: bug disclosure programs reduce vendor notification window from 120 days to 30
control_implications.significance: This finding matters because shortened disclosure deadlines compress vulnerability remediation timelines. Control owners should assess whether current patch management processes can accommodate 30-day disclosure windows and update SLAs accordingly.

paragraphs.text: Supply chain compromises through trusted platforms and remote management tools dominated this period, with attackers exploiting legitimate services like Microsoft SharePoint and GitHub for covert command-and-control, hijacking Optimizely Web Experimentation to inject malicious scripts across 178 organizations, and breaching AI infrastructure provider Fireworks to expose 150,000 Uber driver records. Concurrently, active exploitation of ScreenConnect and N-central remote management platforms continues despite available patches, indicating persistent gaps in third-party extension management and hotfix deployment. Control owners must verify monitoring coverage for anomalous API usage on approved services, validate supplier assurance for critical AI and web service dependencies, and confirm remediation completion for all remote management tool vulnerabilities.

Google Project Zero's decision to slash bug disclosure deadlines from 120 days to 30 over 14 months compresses vulnerability remediation windows across the ecosystem. This change pressures patch management processes to accelerate testing and deployment cycles, particularly for widely deployed platforms like ScreenConnect and N-central where active exploitation persists. Vulnerability management owners should assess current SLA alignment with the new disclosure timeline and document any compensating controls for assets that cannot meet accelerated patching requirements.
